plan: In a second-price auction, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy: you win whenever your value exceeds the highest competing bid, and you pay only that competing bid, ensuring non-negative profit whenever you win. Shading the bid down only reduces the chance of winning profitable auctions without lowering the price paid. Therefore, I will bid exactly my value of $39.

This is a second-price auction (I pay the second-highest bid if I win), which means bidding my true value is the dominant strategy—I never overpay since I only pay what the next-highest bidder bid, and bidding truthfully maximizes my expected profit without risk of winning at a loss or losing a profitable opportunity. With no prior history to suggest otherwise, I'll bid exactly my value of $27.

This is a second-price auction, where bidding your true value is the dominant strategy. Since I pay only the second-highest bid if I win, bidding my actual value of $13 ensures I never overpay and maximizes expected profit regardless of what others bid. Bidding lower risks losing profitable auctions, and bidding higher risks winning at a loss. I'll bid exactly $13.
